title: Mid block: back to halfway
titleKid: Ball past you? Back to halfway
brief: Your team is in a mid block, but you have gone high to press their full-back.
briefKid: Your team waits near halfway. You ran forward to chase their defender.
question: Their #8 has turned and is running at your midfield. Where do you go?
questionKid: Their midfielder got past you with the ball. Where do you go?

takeaway.standard: In a mid block the front players sit around the halfway line, just in front of the midfield: once the ball gets past you, get back there so the block stays short with no space between the lines.
takeaway.kid: When the ball gets past you, run back to halfway, close to your team.

misconceptions.text: You stayed up the pitch after the ball went past you, so your team is split in two with a big gap in front of your midfield.
misconceptions.textKid: You stayed too far up. Run back so there is no big gap.

misconceptions.text: You dropped all the way back to your full-back; one of you is enough there, so stay just in front of your midfield.
misconceptions.textKid: Too far back! Stay just in front of your midfielders.

notes: Authored answer: the engine's best spot is the winger's layer-A spot (about (60.4, 10)), 5 m past the ball and 8 m into their half, which contradicts the lesson (back to halfway, just in front of the midfield, goal-side of the ball). The coach's spot is (54, 11) with a winger zone narrowed to tx 3, so a spot still past the ball drops out of S (the old engine spot scores about 73). stayed-high covers everything from 4 m past the ball up the flank; it holds no S spot. History: the ideal was (58.5, 15.5), then the engine's (60.5, 10).
